must_fix: (criterion 1/4, highest impact, sixth consecutive loop with a new failure type) DA18 found that RMD.md's §5 stated a specific FY2027 guidance range ($5.75-$5.85B revenue, $12.00-$12.25 non-GAAP diluted EPS) that does not exist anywhere in the 8-K it cited as the source -- I independently WebFetched the same ResMed Q4/FY2026 press release and confirmed exactly: no FY2027 revenue or EPS range of any kind is given; the only FY2027 guidance is '>$1.85 billion in capital to be returned to shareholders'; the same release also discloses an agreement to sell the MatrixCare business (closing Q1 FY2027), which the dossier's bull case relied on as a growth segment and never mentioned. This is qualitatively worse than the prior four loops' errors (Loop 5 GM/RJF entity conflation, Loop 6 COR mislabel, Loop 7 PPG sum error, Loop 8 TJX prior-year column): those were mislabelled real numbers, this is a numeric range invented and attributed to a filing that does not contain it, plus a material omitted fact. Neither lead_dossier_precheck.py (WEC/MCK/PTC/RMD flags checked: RMD's only flag is an unrelated entity_scope note about a debt-tag sum, not a guidance check) nor lead_xbrl_crosstie.py (which only compares numeric tags, and a guidance range in prose has no XBRL tag to cross-tie against) could have caught this class of error by construction. To the program's credit, this was caught and fixed before release, not after: RMD was re-assessed, downgraded INCLUDE -> INCLUDE-SMALL and then dropped from the built 20 (CAH restored), with the correction dated and reasoned in RMD.md and STATE.md. Fix: add a pre-publication check that any forward-looking numeric guidance claim must be stored with a verbatim quoted source sentence (not just an accession number), so a reviewer can see at a glance whether the cited text actually contains the number -- a control aimed at fabrication/hallucination specifically, since arithmetic and column checks cannot catch it.

(carried, confirmed by design, seventh consecutive loop) The verification gate reads OPEN for exactly one reason: outputs/c1_consistency.json still narrates the pre-wave-6 build (its own text cites '268 researched / 68 queued / 172 eligible' and the TJX/SO-era holding list, not the current 20: TJX WEC STE MA USB BALL DOV EXC ADP CAH BR MCK PGR AXP HBAN CRH LVS PTC VEEV GDDY, content_sha256 7ac48e4d...). I ran code/lead_verify_gate.py myself and confirmed no holding lacks an independent DA-series fact-check and no FAIL is left uncorrected. This exact gap has now been the sole open item in every loop from 3 through 9; it has still never been observed to read PASS by an outside auditor on the build actually being reviewed.

(minor, criterion 10) STATE.md's wave-6 log entry states '8 names in every ordering (was 14)', but outputs/lead_j_sensitivity.json's in_every_ordering array and FINAL_REPORT.md's §6 text both correctly show 9 (ADP, CAH, CRH, EXC, GDDY, LVS, TJX, USB, VEEV). The published report is right; the internal STATE.md log is the one that is stale/wrong by one. Fix the log line so an internal reader auditing STATE.md against the report does not see a spurious mismatch.
